about.title: A Few Words About Myself.
about.subtitle: ✦ Getting to Know Me
about.text1: Fullstack Developer with 3+ years of coding experience, though my primary expertise lies in frontend development. I work daily with React and Next.js, using TypeScript, Tailwind, and Feature-Sliced Design (FSD) for scalable architectures—opting for a modular approach on smaller projects.
about.text2: That said, I'm equally capable of building complete backend systems from scratch. My server-side stack includes Java, Spring Boot, and PostgreSQL, and I have hands-on experience with Kafka, Redis, Docker, and Kubernetes for microservices and distributed applications. I can confidently deliver full-stack solutions end-to-end.
about.text3: I also design interfaces in Figma from the ground up, because I believe great code deserves great aesthetics.
about.text4: For the past year, I've been working at KillCode studio, handling client-side development in a team environment. I regularly participate in code reviews, collaborate closely with other developers, and follow clean Git workflows. Outside of work, I've mentored fellow developers during their learning journey, helped them grow, and even led small teams on pet projects.
about.text5: I'm looking for ambitious projects where I can contribute both as a frontend specialist or as a fullstack developer—ideally in a strong team that values clean code, thoughtful design, and real engineering challenges.

overview.title: Overview
overview.content: Explore With Me is a platform for discovering events and coordinating people who want to attend them. Built from scratch as my graduate diploma project, it's a complete microservices REST application: users create events, discover others' events via search filters, and request to join; admins moderate everything.

stack.title: Tech stack
stack.option4: Docker Compose (4 containers: two apps + two DB)
stack.option5: Maven (multi‑module assembly), Lombok, Spring Boot Actuator
stack.option6: Code quality: Checkstyle, SpotBugs, JaCoCo (coverage threshold in the assembly)

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.paragraph1: Two microservices as separate Maven modules. The main service (port 8080) handles all business logic — users, events, categories, compilations, participation requests and comments. A dedicated stats service (port 9090) records page hits and aggregates view counters; the main service calls it over HTTP through its own REST client and enriches events with live view data. Each service has its own PostgreSQL database, and everything deploys with a single docker compose up.
architecture.paragraph2: Access control follows URL conventions: admin endpoints (/admin), user endpoints (/users/{id}), and read-only public endpoints that only expose published data.

functional.title: Key features
functional.option1: Event management with a full lifecycle. Users create events and send them for review; admins publish or reject them. Edge cases are handled: moderation only from the PENDING state, no editing after publication, events must start at least 2 hours ahead.
functional.option2: Search & sorting. Public catalog with full-text search (annotation + description), filters for categories, paid/free, date range, and "only available places". Sorting by event date or by views, counted live from the stats service (including unique-by-IP).
functional.option3: Participation requests. Join events respecting participant limits; auto-approval for events without moderation; cancel own requests; bulk approve/reject for the owner.
functional.option4: Compilations - pinned and regular event collections managed by admins.
functional.option5: Comments - my own extension beyond the original spec: commenting only on published events, author-only editing, admin moderation/deletion.
functional.option6: Categories & users, location deduplication by coordinates, consistent pagination, and a unified error handler with correct HTTP semantics (400/404/409).

decisions.title: Engineering notes
decisions.option1: JPA Specifications for flexible filter combinations
decisions.option2: DB schema versioned in the repo via schema.sql instead of Hibernate-generated DDL
decisions.option3: CI-quality gates - Checkstyle on every build, SpotBugs, and JaCoCo coverage thresholds.
decisions.paragraph1: The project shows a full microservices journey: from data modeling and cross-service integration to error handling and containerized deployment with disciplined code quality.

overview.title: Overview
overview.content: KillCode Studio is a conversion-focused landing page and portfolio for a software development studio: the site presents the studio's services, workflow, and client cases while doubling as a live showcase of real projects. It was built from scratch on a modern stack and shipped to production — responsive, bilingual, and animated in nearly every section.

stack.title: Технологический стек
stack.option6: Code quality: strict TypeScript (verbatimModuleSyntax), ESLint with React rules, unified Prettier formatting

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.content: The project uses a feature-based structure. Each feature (hero, products, portfolio, contacts, etc.) lives in its own folder with its components, hooks, and types, while reusable entities are extracted into shared (icons, images, the i18n context, and utilities). Section data — services, growth steps, portfolio cases — is not scattered across components: it is re-derived from the active language through memoized hooks, which kept adding new sections and translations predictable.

functional.title: Key features
functional.option1: Five-section landing. A hero with an animated editor window, a typewriter effect, and Python syntax highlighting; infinite CSS marquee carousels of services; an advantages block; an animated studio-growth timeline; and an interactive "how to order" diagram with an SVG stroke-draw line and step markers.
functional.option2: A 12-case portfolio. Every case ships with an image, a price in USD, and its stack: a banking RAG platform, a Go + WebSocket marketplace CRM, VPN infrastructure, Aiogram Telegram bots, parsers, and Figma design.
functional.option3: Full RU/EN localization. A custom, fully typed i18n system: language is resolved from localStorage and browser settings and switched with a header dropdown; all content — including portfolio data — lives in locale dictionaries.
functional.option4: Contact form. Validation via react-hook-form + yup with localized error messages, async submission to an API through axios with an auth key, and full loading/success/error state handling.
functional.option5: SEO & responsiveness. Per-page title and meta via react-helmet-async, robots.txt, sitemap, and favicon configured; every landing section has a dedicated mobile variant.

decisions.title: Engineering notes
decisions.option1: A typed i18n dictionary contract means any missing key between RU and EN is caught at compile time.
decisions.option2: The validation schema is rebuilt per language, so error translations live in one place.
decisions.option3: Animations are driven by react-intersection-observer — elements reveal as they enter the viewport instead of firing on timers.
decisions.option4: Сustom keyframe animations and the brand palette are centralized in Tailwind's @theme.
decisions.paragraph1: The project shows how to build a modern production site from scratch — from data structure and a localization system to responsiveness and living animations — without sacrificing code cleanliness or maintainability.
